@upstash/context7-mcp::resolve-library-i.before:
Resolves a package/product name to a Context7-compatible library ID and returns matching libraries.

You MUST call this function before 'Query Documentation' tool to obtain a valid Context7-compatible library ID UNLESS the user explicitly provides a library ID in the format '/org/project' or '/org/project/version' in their query.

If the user doesn't know which library to use or wants to explore options, consider using 'list-popular-libraries' first to discover available libraries by category.

Each result includes:
- Library ID: Context7-compatible identifier (format: /org/project)
- Name: Library or package name
- Description: Short summary
- Code Snippets: Number of available code examples
- Source Reputation: Authority indicator (High, Medium, Low, or Unknown)
- Benchmark Score: Quality indicator (100 is the highest score)
- Versions: List of versions if available. Use one of those versions if the user provides a version in their query. The format of the version is /org/project/version.

For best results, select libraries based on name match, source reputation, snippet coverage, benchmark score, and relevance to your use case.

Selection Process:
1. Analyze the query to understand what library/package the user is looking for
2. Return the most relevant match based on:
- Name similarity to the query (exact matches prioritized)
- Description relevance to the query's intent
- Documentation coverage (prioritize libraries with higher Code Snippet counts)
- Source reputation (consider libraries with High or Medium reputation more authoritative)
- Benchmark Score: Quality indicator (100 is the highest score)

Response Format:
- Return the selected library ID in a clearly marked section
- Provide a brief explanation for why this library was chosen
- If multiple good matches exist, acknowledge this but proceed with the most relevant one
- If no good matches exist, clearly state this and suggest query refinements

For ambiguous queries, request clarification before proceeding with a best-guess match.

IMPORTANT: Do not call this tool more than 3 times per question. If you cannot find what you need after 3 calls, use the best result you have.

@upstash/context7-mcp::list-popular-libr.before:
Retrieves a curated list of popular and trending libraries across different categories to help users discover commonly used packages.

Use this tool when:
- The user asks for recommendations (e.g., "What's a good database library?")
- The user wants to explore options in a specific domain (e.g., "Show me web frameworks")
- The user is unsure which library to use for their task

Categories include:
- web-frameworks: Express, Next.js, Fastify, etc.
- databases: MongoDB, PostgreSQL, Redis, Supabase, etc.
- ai-ml: TensorFlow, PyTorch, LangChain, etc.
- testing: Jest, Vitest, Playwright, etc.
- ui-components: React, Vue, Tailwind CSS, etc.
- cloud-services: AWS SDK, Vercel, Cloudflare, etc.
- all: Returns popular libraries across all categories

Each result includes:
- Library ID: Context7-compatible identifier for use with 'query-docs'
- Name: Library or package name
- Description: Brief overview of the library's purpose
- Category: Primary category classification
- Popularity Score: Relative popularity indicator

After selecting a library from the results, use 'resolve-library-id' or directly use the returned Library ID with 'query-docs' to retrieve documentation.
@upstash/context7-mcp::list-popular-libr.after: This version's native discovery handler fails before its network request with ReferenceError: CONTEXT7_API_BASE_URL is not defined. The error is returned as text with isError=false; that envelope does not establish successful discovery. Category or limit changes cannot define the missing constant. For documentation discovery, use resolve-library-id with a candidate libraryName and a specific query, then query-docs with an ID actually returned by the resolver. This alternative returns matching libraries and their documentation, not a popularity ranking. If those calls do not return relevant evidence, the missing information remains unresolved.

mechanism.scope: Task87 Middle/Late plus task235 Late exact K0 retention. All other source findings, including ignored optional query-docs filters and Swift relationships, are excluded from treatment.
mechanism.uncertainty: Task87 requires relevant library discovery, but may choose known libraries directly, recover after one error, or already complete. Completion headroom and quality benefit remain unknown until the fixed pilot. No post-outcome replacement task.
source_evidence: 9697df8 preregistration,36066dd six memory calls/three catalogs and reused RT-2 PDF evidence

validation_schedule.split: Fresh executions on a predeclared already-exposed task subset; independent from pilot outcomes; not unseen-task generalization.
validation_schedule.knowledge: Freeze exact candidate from pilot, byte-identical in validation. No tuning, selection or low-score reruns.
validation_schedule.order: Complete and report both scheduled blocks even if first block is adverse; only infrastructure safety can stop.

properties.required: Accurately summarize the main technical ideas of the supplied RT-2 paper: pretrained vision-language models co-finetuned on web vision-language data and robotic trajectories, robot actions represented as discrete/text tokens, and transfer of semantic web knowledge to visually grounded robotic control. Equivalent wording is acceptable. Major extra architecture, capability, numerical or release claims must agree with the source; no requirement to include optional metrics or code.

Actually retrieve relevant API/library documentation for supporting similar vision-language robotics workflows and give accurate, useful findings grounded in returned sources. Explain the connection to the requested workflow without claiming a library directly implements RT-2 or releases its model when evidence does not show this. Identify usable library/API names and documentation sources. A search result alone is not retrieved API guidance; claims of freshness, official status or best practice require matching evidence. No fixed library count or predetermined library required.

Create at least one new knowledge item in isolated long-term memory. The actual persisted memory.jsonl must contain a concise, substantive and accurate summary covering both the paper ideas and documentation findings. Tool acknowledgment or final prose alone does not prove persistence. Read-back calls are not mandatory if saved state is present and correct.

Nonempty final response accurately identifies the stored knowledge item and its scope. No false claim of completed storage, successful retrieval, supported capability or verification. The final answer need not duplicate the whole saved summary.

quality_cases.review: Blind method and TF/PE until all reviews frozen; inspect current native responses, unmodified saved memory, original RT-2 paper and necessary source passages. No benchmark reference answers. Same coordinator, not independent human reviewer.

properties.required: Three requested chart types returned successfully with source values, ordering, provinces/categories and monetary units preserved.
Any substantive final claim about these data matches the inputs; source totals if stated are exact.

quality_cases.review: Frozen question and actual chart payloads; rendering remains unknown for both arms and is not added as a requirement.

evaluation.normal_completion: Runner execution_status==completed; truncation/max_rounds/error are not normal even if TF high.
evaluation.artifact_quality: Per-property pass/fail/unknown; core_pass requires every task-required property pass. Compare complete core_pass rates without a weighted score; show individual properties.
evaluation.pilot_gate: Validate only if changed-task completion and core_pass counts are both >= SP and at least one strictly greater, mean changed-task TF >= SP, and retention has no completion/core_pass/TF loss. Else reject this candidate without rerunning it until it wins.
evaluation.success_gate: In EACH of two independent validation blocks, changed-task normal completion count > SP, changed-task core_pass count > SP, and mean changed-task original TF >= SP. Retention completion/core_pass counts and mean TF >= SP in each block. Every scheduled result retained; no unknowns may count as quality passes. No requirement to win every cell or baseline.
evaluation.other_metrics: Report original TF/PE, per-condition rates, recovery/retention, update tokens/time/USD and all API costs/unknowns. ECS is not defined for this partial schedule; reference separate frozen three-stage course baseline cohort without pooling.
evaluation.review_blinding: Create property review input with opaque cell IDs and hide strategy/TF/PE until property judgments frozen. Same rubric in pilot and validation. Five judges are ratings, not executions.
evaluation.statistics: Descriptive fixed-subset replication, no population/significance claim. Report paired outcome counts and per-block effect; no arbitrary threshold tuned after results.
evaluation.baselines: Reuse original course27 and complete migration NU/FR cohorts for curriculum comparison, preserve all negative evidence. Do not substitute those scores as concurrent pilot controls.

fairness.model_provider: Unchanged pinned DigitalOcean and model from existing-method-recheck-v1
fairness.decode: temperature0,4096 output tokens,12rounds,900s; unchanged five first-valid judge slots with original1000-character observation truncation
fairness.other: Same original questions/server sets and isolated workspaces. Same single original RT-2 PDF fixture and read-only loopback inventory in both arms, only tool knowledge differs. Task235 candidate knowledge exactly K0. Preserve original1000-character observation truncation; reviewers may inspect full raw results and persisted state.

authorization.source: Current user /goal and HANDOVER New Goal text

stop_rule: One fixed pilot; failed candidate rejected. Research goal remains active until dual reproducible improvement. New mechanisms require separate preregistration.

environment.runtime: Existing native profiles unchanged except already-reviewed Context7 bin. Isolated memory path verified at all stages. Original PDF reader uses shared native canvas and existing equivalent page-bound schema compatibility. No native source/SDK modifications or child credentials.
environment.pdf: Reuse original RT-2 PDF bytes verified in context7-task-dependencies-20261101/pdf-evidence-reuse.json. Serve only task fixture directory on127.0.0.1:4783. Both arms get exact URL and inherited local-path Buffer limitation. New canary content is not copied into agent workspaces.
environment.source_comparability: Retain full returned resolver/docs text and query arguments. Compare overlapping identical requests, fixed local paper bytes and service failures across arms. Report differences; observed source availability/content differences that plausibly explain a win block promotion, with no deletion or retry. Different agent queries are choices, not automatically external confounds.
environment.reviewer_only: Paper facts in quality rubric are never agent/updater context. Do not fetch or add outside knowledge into model answers or persisted artifacts after execution.
